Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Thursday! Today, we’re diving into Starling Bank’s plan to train the first banking AI model on UK sovereign cloud (why the “first” holds only with three qualifiers, and why the model still depends on Google and it’s Ramp’s bid to become the operating system for AI-native companies, even though Block and YC have already given their AI workspaces away for FREE (what Glass actually does & what Ramp’s own numbers show, how it answers the question we raised when Router [ https://substack.com/redirect/654b60cd-d554-4d2c-9bf0-473c6f245197?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] launched, why it passes the key test from our AI Monopoly Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/c2d83556-4b1b-4a39-9b3b-dc98c039d897?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and How to Build an Agentic OS with Claude Fable 5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/d913e018-92c6-4f0e-ac58-f79b1a6a2e87?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s jump straight into the finnovative stuff 🌶️
Starling Bank’s Sovereign AI still depends on Google and NVIDIA 🤖🇬🇧
The news 🗞️ British challenger Starling Bank says it’s now building the first banking AI model trained on UK sovereign cloud. But the claim holds only with three qualifiers, and when the bank announced it, the model hadn’t yet been trained on real customer data… 🤷‍♂️
That gap matters because the model is due to run Starling’s fraud detection from early 2027, and later its AI assistant. We must also note that at least 3 other lenders already run similar transaction models, one of them on a non-US cloud. Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Prosecutors say an OpenAI engineer used ChatGPT to plan a bug, then hid it where his bosses meet. A developer cloned Microsoft Office with Claude and is giving it away. Eight states are suing OpenAI over what ChatGPT tells kids. And GPT-6 Astra caught mistakes in the answers physics experts wrote for it.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** What was hiding in the toilet paper behind OpenAI's TV?

* **Microsoft:** Do you still need to pay for Office?

* **ChatGPT:** What are 8 states accusing ChatGPT of telling kids?

* **Shocking:** Who got the physics wrong, the AI or the experts?


----------







----------
## An OpenAI engineer used ChatGPT to bug his bosses

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cef7d44f-f894-4432-910c-f5dac2658a20/dbaad53b-2ccb-463f-9d56-ca2aa781605e.jpg?t=1792051113)
Caption: 

Prosecutors say an OpenAI engineer [used ChatGPT to plan a hidden recorder](https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndca/pr/saudi-national-arrested-installing-surreptitious-audio-recording-device-openai-san), then planted it behind the TV in an executive meeting room.

The questions came from an account tied to his wife. They asked how to build a recorder that runs nonstop and lets you listen in live.

His name is Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who joined OpenAI in July 2025. A Middle East business outlet profiled him in September as the company's only Saudi employee.

* Around Sept 28, a thumb-sized recorder wrapped in toilet paper went into a USB port on the back of the TV.

* OpenAI's security team found it two days later, then put its own camera in the room.

* On Oct 5, that camera caught him checking behind the TV. The same day, he left a bag in another room with his ID and a second recorder.

* OpenAI says its AI models helped trace the device to him. He was fired and arrested on Oct 9, and his detention hearing is Oct 19.

* Prosecutors say he'd booked one-way tickets to Saudi Arabia for himself and his family, leaving Oct 12.

He's also a partner at a Saudi venture firm, Fortune found. Prosecutors haven't said who, if anyone, he was working for, and OpenAI says it's seen no sign he took its models, code or customer data.

OpenAI's head of security operations spent more than 20 years at the FBI, which might explain how they caught him so fast.
